note: Schmelzer: Sacro-profanus and Duodena sonatas titled 'Sonata a N No. n' (the print's numbering) with the collection as set; keys only where a recording or IMSLP gives them. Gap check from de.wikipedia's work list: Serenata con altre arie a 5, Balletti a 4 and a 5, Sonata a 8 per chiesa e camera and the Sonata a 3 for violin, clarino and trombone are recorded but their exact scorings (bass/continuo) were not confirmed, so not added. Uccellini: Op. 3/4 pieces kept only where a recording names the piece; 'a 3' pieces with 'basso' get a cello beside the continuo, as IMSLP lists a separate bass part. The Op. 9 sinfonie (not on IMSLP) are attributed to Op. 9 from the Manze album; the Clematis tracks' opus is inferred, not printed. Pachelbel: the Aria con variazioni in A major, P. 28 (recorded by Musica Antiqua Köln) and the Suite in F-sharp minor, P. 449, were not added: their scorings (Wikipedia: 'vn, 2vg'; 'vn, 2va, b.c.') could not be confirmed against an edition and no recording of P. 449 was found. Locke: the Broken Consort and Little Consort suites are given as three viols (IMSLP's editions) with violins as printed alternatives; the Locke Consort plays Part I on violins with continuo. Broken Consort Part II (5 suites) is not on IMSLP: its scoring is assumed to match Part I. Tripla Concordia (1677) is an anthology and was not added. Rosenmüller: the 1682 sonatas' bass part is IMSLP's 'viol/bassoon' (given as viola da gamba, bassoon as alternative). Studentenmusik (1654; recorded by The King's Noyse) is for unspecified 3 or 5 parts and was not added. Evidence comes from Apple Music (iTunes Search API) track lists, MusicBrainz works and IMSLP; Presto and Naxos were not consulted. Levels are estimates from the scoring and recordings, not from reading the scores. Uccellini's Op. 7 No. 18 rests on a single MusicBrainz recording with no performer listed (confidence low).
